title: stickypatch config
description: Local patches for installed npm packages that survive updates.

text.description: A string, an array of lines (joined with \n), or { "file": "path relative to the config" }.

name.description: Label for this target (defaults to the package name).

package.description: npm package name, e.g. @openai/codex. Located automatically.

bin.description: Command name used to find the copy on PATH, if it differs from the package name.

testedVersions.description: Versions you have verified these patches against. apply refuses others unless --approve / --allow-untested.

restart.description: Shell command run by --restart after apply/rollback.

health.description: How --restart decides the service came back. A URL string, a command string, or an object.

delay.description: Seconds to wait before the first probe (default 1).

busy.description: Shell command that exits 0 when it is safe to restart (e.g. no active sessions).

denyEnv.description: If any of these env vars is set, write commands refuse (read-only context, e.g. an AI agent session).

why.description: What this patch fixes. Shown to reviewers (human or AI) after updates.

file.description: Path relative to the package root.

find.description: Exact text that must occur exactly once.

marker.description: Text whose presence means 'applied' (defaults to replace).

previous.description: Older forms of replace; apply migrates them.

upstream.description: Evidence that upstream now ships this fix. All conditions must hold.

retired.description: Set by `stickypatch retire`. Retired patches are kept as a record but never checked or applied.
